rubric.evidence: MDN WebTransport/reliability (modified 2026-08-27) and WebTransport/supportsReliableOnly_static (modified 2026-10-12) read via their index.json on 2026-11-15: both have Value, Examples, Specifications and Browser compatibility sections, so this is a Case A stub per routine Step 5 (coverage is unambiguous, so invariant #6 does not force a generated page). The IDL quoted in the quick reference is verbatim from the W3C TR WebTransport IDL (Candidate Recommendation Snapshot). The Chrome-specific behaviour section is taken from Chromium trunk: web_transport.idl gates both members with [RuntimeEnabled=WebTransportReliability]; web_transport.h initialises reliability_ to kPending; web_transport.cc assigns kSupportsUnreliable once, immediately before ready_->ResolveWithUndefined(), and supportsReliableOnly() returns false; web_transport_options.idl has no requireUnreliable member. runtime_enabled_features.json5 has WebTransportReliability status stable.
rubric.notes: Spec rule (reliability left 'pending' when establishment fails) comes from the TR 'process a WebTransport fetch response' steps: [[Reliability]] is assigned only on the success path.

rubric.evidence: Feature id 5094058497277952 appears in the live milestone=158 listing under 'Enabled by default' with listing name 'WebTransport reliability attributes' (fetched 2026-11-15); slug derived from that name per invariant #1, folder placed per invariant #2. The detail record's stale 'Proposed' status text is disclosed on the page.

Adds what MDN does not track: Chromium's actual values (never 'reliable-only', supportsReliableOnly hard-coded false, stays 'pending' on failure), requireUnreliable missing from Chromium's options IDL, the runtime flag, intents, WPT files, and the BCD-vs-ChromeStatus disagreements.

One short Chrome-specific feature-detection snippet in a semantic pre/code block (the &&, quotes and comments are HTML-escaped where needed). Fuller worked examples are left to MDN's two pages and the three showcase concepts.

The compat table is built from raw BCD api/WebTransport.json (main, 2026-11-15): reliability chrome 157 / firefox 114 / safari 26.4; supportsReliableOnly_static chrome 157 / firefox 158 / safari 26.4; WebTransport.options_requireUnreliable_parameter chrome false / firefox 114 / safari 26.4. Baseline comes from api.webstatus.dev/v1/features/webtransport (newly, low_date 2026-03-24). BCD tags only reliability into that web-feature, so the page says supportsReliableOnly has no Baseline status of its own.
rubric.notes: The ChromeStatus availability_expectation says Firefox implements only reliability, which contradicts BCD; this is disclosed.

rubric.evidence: Single h1 and main landmark. The quick-reference table uses th scope=row; the compat table has thead with scope=col, row headers and an accessible name via aria-labelledby. Both scroll wrappers are role=region with tabindex=0 so keyboard users can scroll them. All colours come from shared design-system tokens; no raw hex.

Playwright screenshots were read at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3. The first mobile pass found two defects, both fixed in place: lede code tokens split mid-word (shortened to the member names), and the 4-column compat table crushed so headers broke mid-word (now min-width 34rem inside the .table-wrap scroller, with overflow-wrap normal, and the caption moved outside the scroller so it is not clipped). Final: scrollWidth equals viewport on both classes; zero console errors and zero failed requests; deno task responsive reports desktop ok and mobile ok.

The CPS feature index and its three concept routes (reliability-readout, transport-strategy-picker, readonly-and-static-edges) were each HEAD-checked 200 on 2026-11-15 and are linked from the quick reference. The first own-feature link, the reliability-readout concept, is the manifest's selected demo. As a Case A stub the page follows the house shape and links the demos rather than embedding an iframe.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive two-column reference table with long code tokens and URLs on 360px mobile without horizontal page overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic table headers. Put an overflow:auto wrapper around the table, with tabindex=0, role=region and an accessible name. Keep cell text legible instead of letting columns shrink below readability.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied. Both tables sit in .table-wrap role=region tabindex=0 (one with aria-label, one with aria-labelledby). The compat table has thead/scope=col and row headers, and gets min-width:34rem plus overflow-wrap:normal so it scrolls inside its region instead of breaking headers mid-word. Exception: no sticky headers or container-query stacking, because these are 3-4 row tables where sticky context adds nothing.
